title: Session resumption and token-trim reconciliation to prevent duplicated/partial tokens
text:
Session resumption and token-trim reconciliation to prevent duplicated/partial tokens

description:
Post-incident follow-up from the 2025-02-07 cross-region capacity event where a subset of streaming sessions observed client disconnects followed by resumed responses that contained duplicated or truncated tokens. Affected clients reported partial UTF-8 sequences and repeated prefixes leading to corrupted outputs for chat and streaming generation endpoints. This ticket drives engineering work to (1) ensure session-resume is idempotent at token boundaries, (2) sanitize partial token fragments on reconnect, and (3) harden backpressure interactions so soft closes do not leave sessions in an inconsistent commit state.

root_cause:
During a rapid capacity contraction, runtime backpressure logic issued a soft-close that allowed the runtime to drop remaining in-flight token fragments without a durable commit. Clients reconnecting to a routed replica negotiated resume based on wall-clock offsets rather than sequence-anchored token positions. Combined with a subtle KV-cache eviction race, resumed sessions replayed overlapping token prefixes or emitted half tokens when buffer flushes coincided with partial UTF-8 sequences.

impact_summary:
Approximately 3% of streaming sessions across the EU-west region for a 12 minute window produced corrupted outputs. Two customers reported production failures; no secrets were exfiltrated. Incidence correlated with high request spikes and node deprovisioning events.

actions:
Add sequence-numbered token-commit protocol: emit monotonic token_seq and require server-side durable commit before returning final chunk (owner: Liam O'Connor, ETA: 2025-03-08)
Implement reconnect handshake: client provides last-seen token_seq and server responds with canonical resume point (owner: Priya Raman, ETA: 2025-03-12)
Sanitize partial bytes on reconnect: trim incomplete UTF-8 codepoints at the buffer boundary and ensure tokenizer boundary alignment (owner: Mateo Alvarez, ETA: 2025-03-05)
KV-cache eviction guard: prevent eviction of prefix segments while in-flight sessions have resume windows (owner: Runtime team, ETA: 2025-03-10)
Backpressure soft-close change: convert immediate soft-close to drain-with-timeout semantics and send explicit session-closure marker (owner: Anika Shah, ETA: 2025-03-07)
Add end-to-end chaos tests (network partition + node drain) that assert no duplicated tokens on reconnection (owner: SRE, ETA: 2025-03-20)
Dashboard and alerting: add metric stream.session_resume_failures and alert at >0.5% per minute (owner: Observability team, ETA: 2025-03-04)

status_updates:
2025-02-11 - Anika Shah: Collected initial traces and sample payloads from affected sessions. Confirmed duplicated prefixes correspond to overlapping token_seq values under concurrent resume attempts.
2025-02-13 - Liam O'Connor: Reproduced partial-byte truncation locally by simulating a soft-close during token emit; attached unit test harness in repo branch runtime/resume-sim.
2025-02-18 - Mateo Alvarez: Proposed token boundary sanitization approach: use tokenizer's longest-prefix alignment and fallback to base64-escape of incomplete sequences in worst-case. Shared design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/infra/pages/GRACEFUL-RESUME
2025-02-21 - Priya Raman: Design review with PM and SRE; agreed on sequence-numbered commit and reconnect handshake. Minor trade-off: small extra metadata per chunk vs guaranteed idempotence.
2025-02-25 - Runtime team: Implemented soft-close drain change in dev branch; initial load test shows 0.2% increase in median tail latency under high-concurrency but eliminates partial tokens in the test harness.
2025-02-28 - Observability: Drafted alert and Grafana panel for session_resume_failures; PR for alerting: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/410
2025-03-01 - Anika Shah: Merged initial sanitization code and added e2e replay tests; candidate change queued for runtime-1.20 canary.

acceptance_criteria:
All streaming generators must include token_seq on each chunk and persist commit state to local durable store
Resume handshake must return canonical resume_token_seq and not accept offsets older than resume window
No customer-facing corruption reports in the subsequent 3 maintenance windows (observed 0 errors in canary for 48 hours)
Automated chaos tests for node drain and network flaps pass in CI

follow_up:
Coordinate Dedicated engineering and Customer Success to notify the two affected customers with remediation steps and offer a compensated re-run of critical prompts (owner: Customer Success, ETA: 2025-03-05)
Backport hotfix to runtime-1.19 for customers on older pinned runtimes if requested (owner: Release team, ETA: decision by 2025-03-10)
Schedule a cross-team retro to formalize runbook changes for capacity contraction events (owner: SRE, ETA: 2025-03-12)

notes:
Trade-offs considered: increasing chunk metadata increases wire bytes (small %) but simplifies idempotence and allows for cheaper reconciliation on reconnect.
Tokenizer complexity: For multi-language prompts we must ensure language-specific tokenizers are consulted for boundary alignment; this was added to the design doc.
Long-term: Evaluate prefix-proof receipts (Merkle-style) for extremely high-throughput customers where replay risk is unacceptable.
